events.title: An earthquake in the Apennines shakes Rome and Spoleto
events.description: An earthquake originating in the Central Apennines was felt in Rome and Spoleto and damaged the basilica of San Paolo Fuori le Mura. It was recorded in two independent contemporary sources, Einhard's Royal Frankish Annals and the Liber Pontificalis.
events.html: An earthquake originating in the Central Apennines was felt in Rome and Spoleto and damaged the basilica of San Paolo Fuori le Mura. It was recorded in two independent contemporary sources, Einhard's Royal Frankish Annals and the Liber Pontificalis.

events.title: Alexios I Komnenos crushes the Pechenegs at Levounion
events.description: Emperor Alexios I Komnenos and his Cuman allies destroyed an invading Pecheneg horde at Levounion in Thrace, near the mouth of the Maritsa. The victory ended the Pecheneg danger to the Byzantine Empire for a generation.
events.html: Emperor Alexios I Komnenos and his Cuman allies destroyed an invading Pecheneg horde at Levounion in Thrace, near the mouth of the Maritsa. The victory ended the Pecheneg danger to the Byzantine Empire for a generation.

events.title: Joan of Arc enters besieged Orléans
events.description: Joan of Arc entered Orléans with supplies and reinforcements. Within ten days the English abandoned the siege, a turning point in the Hundred Years' War.
events.html: Joan of Arc entered Orléans with supplies and reinforcements. Within ten days the English abandoned the siege, a turning point in the Hundred Years' War.

events.title: The Crown of Castile completes the conquest of Gran Canaria
events.description: After a five-year war, Castile under Queen Isabella I took Gran Canaria from the Canarii who had long lived there, and the Canarian queen Abenchara was captured and imprisoned. The conquest was an important step in the expansion of a unified Spain.
events.html: After a five-year war, Castile under Queen Isabella I took Gran Canaria from the Canarii who had long lived there, and the Canarian queen Abenchara was captured and imprisoned. The conquest was an important step in the expansion of a unified Spain.

events.title: The expulsion of the Jews is announced in Zaragoza
events.description: The Crown's decision to expel the Jews was announced to the procurators of the Kingdom of Aragon in Zaragoza, two days before the edict was proclaimed in Castile. Most of the city's Jews left between 27 and 29 July for exile.
events.html: The Crown's decision to expel the Jews was announced to the procurators of the Kingdom of Aragon in Zaragoza, two days before the edict was proclaimed in Castile. Most of the city's Jews left between 27 and 29 July for exile.

events.title: Gustav Vasa's Swedish troops defeat a Danish force at Västerås
events.description: On Badelundaåsen, northeast of Västerås, Swedish troops led by Gustav Vasa defeated a Danish force under Didrik Slagheck and took the town. Their war deposed King Christian II from the Swedish throne and effectively ended the Kalmar Union.
events.html: On Badelundaåsen, northeast of Västerås, Swedish troops led by Gustav Vasa defeated a Danish force under Didrik Slagheck and took the town. Their war deposed King Christian II from the Swedish throne and effectively ended the Kalmar Union.

events.title: James Cook lands at Botany Bay
events.description: The crew of HMS Endeavour made the first recorded European landing on Australia's east coast, meeting resistance from Gweagal men. The bay was named for the plants collected by Joseph Banks.
events.html: The crew of HMS Endeavour made the first recorded European landing on Australia's east coast, meeting resistance from Gweagal men. The bay was named for the plants collected by Joseph Banks.

events.title: British garrison surrenders to the Ottomans at Kut
events.description: After a siege of nearly five months, General Charles Townshend surrendered some 13,000 British and Indian troops at Kut al-Amara in Mesopotamia. Thousands died in captivity.
events.html: After a siege of nearly five months, General Charles Townshend surrendered some 13,000 British and Indian troops at Kut al-Amara in Mesopotamia. Thousands died in captivity.

events.title: US troops liberate Dachau
events.description: American soldiers entered Dachau, the first concentration camp, opened in 1933. They found more than 30,000 prisoners and thousands of bodies.
events.html: American soldiers entered Dachau, the first concentration camp, opened in 1933. They found more than 30,000 prisoners and thousands of bodies.

events.title: Cyclone strikes the coast of Bangladesh
events.description: A severe tropical cyclone drove a storm surge of up to six metres onto the Chittagong coast, killing some 138,000 people. It led to wider investment in cyclone shelters and warnings.
events.html: A severe tropical cyclone drove a storm surge of up to six metres onto the Chittagong coast, killing some 138,000 people. It led to wider investment in cyclone shelters and warnings.

events.title: Rioting erupts in Los Angeles after the Rodney King verdict
events.description: Riots began after four police officers were acquitted of beating Rodney King. Over six days more than 60 people died and damage reached about $1 billion.
